deviations: Anderson (2008) indices built as: items standardized by control-group (born 1956+) mean and SD, inverse-covariance (row-sum) weights from the covariance of the standardized items over complete cases, index re-standardized to control mean 0 / SD 1; computed once on the full respondent sample (not within the bandwidth). The authors' _gweightave2.ado was not available, so the exact weighting/normalization may differ.
notes: Spec: feols(y ~ before1955 + dif + dif:before1955 + female | birth month + province + surveyor + education + ethnicity), |dif| <= 45 months, uniform kernel, SEs clustered by month-year of birth (modate), survey non-respondents dropped. Attempts 1-2 were exploratory (variable listing; sample-size counts showing |dif|<=45 with complete controls reproduces 1214/1222/1203/1133 exactly). Attempt 3 was the first estimating run; fixest dropped fixed-effect singletons (N=1199 etc.). check_attempt reported all claims within tolerance, but I had compared N with Table 3 myself, so the final run (singletons kept, fixef.rm='none', as dummy-variable OLS in Stata does) is recorded after a claim attempt. Final: mobility coefficients, SRQ-20 sum and all Ns match the paper (SEs too: 0.180, 0.045, 0.036, 0.440); the three Anderson indices come out lower than published (0.157 vs 0.205, 0.112 vs 0.175, 0.152 vs 0.158) although their samples match, so the index construction differs in a detail I could not recover from the text; I did not tune it to the claims.
